skill.name: verification-protocol
skill.description: Requires an independent verifier to check task completion with evidence, retry failures, and escalate unresolved work.
skill.summary: Evidence-first protocol for verifying AI agent task completion.

content.value_statement: AI agents can mark work complete without proof, which creates false completion risk. This skill requires independent evidence before task completion is accepted.
actual_capabilities: Defines an independent verification workflow for agent task completion claims.
Lists evidence checks for files, placeholders, compilation, linting, tests, and endpoints.
Shows pass and fail evidence formats for verification results.
Defines retry handling and escalation after repeated verification failures.
Provides orchestration examples for accepting verified results only.
limitations: It is a Markdown protocol, not a runnable verifier implementation.
It requires a separate verifier agent or orchestrator to enforce decisions.
Examples assume JavaScript and TypeScript project tooling.
It does not define path sandboxing or command allowlists.

use_cases.title: Enforce Evidence-Based Completion
use_cases.description: Engineering leads can require proof before AI-generated work is marked complete.

use_cases.title: Audit AI Generated Changes
use_cases.description: QA reviewers can compare claims against concrete file, test, and lint evidence.

use_cases.title: Integrate Verifier Workflows
use_cases.description: Platform teams can add independent verification and escalation rules to agent orchestration.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Completion Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of one claimed task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use verification-protocol to review this completion claim. List evidence for each criterion and decide whether the task is verified.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Claimed Outputs
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of files and checks.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply verification-protocol to these claimed outputs: [files]. Check file existence, placeholders, compile status, lint status, and tests. Report failures with evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Verifier Flow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced setup for an agent pipeline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a verifier workflow for our agent pipeline. Include evidence capture, retry limits, escalation rules, and result logging.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Failed Verification
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of repeated verification failures.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this verification failure history. Identify repeated failure types, missing evidence, and when a human reviewer should decide.

output_examples.input: An agent says a new TypeScript feature and its tests are complete.
output_examples.output: Not verified. The feature file exists, but tests fail and placeholder markers remain. The agent should fix those issues and resubmit.

output_examples.input: An orchestrator needs a completion rule for AI generated changes.
output_examples.output: Completion requires independent evidence for each criterion. The task remains open when evidence is missing or any required check fails.

output_examples.input: A team wants to reduce false successful task reports.
output_examples.output: Use a separate verifier, store proof for each check, and escalate after repeated failures.

best_practices: Use a verifier that did not produce the work.
Capture concrete evidence for every criterion before marking completion.
Escalate repeated failures instead of relaxing criteria.
anti_patterns: Accepting an agent completion claim without evidence.
Skipping slow tests or lint checks and marking success anyway.
Treating vague success text as proof of completion.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies task completion claims by requiring independent evidence for each stated completion criterion.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a Markdown protocol with examples for implementation.

faq.question: Does it support Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: Can it verify non-code work?
faq.answer: Yes, if clear criteria and evidence methods are defined before verification starts.

faq.question: Who should perform verification?
faq.answer: A separate agent or reviewer should verify the work, not the agent that completed it.

faq.question: How are failures handled?
faq.answer: Failures return to the agent with evidence. After repeated failures, the task should escalate to human review.
